title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: a computation in Grothendieck's notes for his 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex. (The neighbouring pages in the scan are unrelated typescript from SGA 7 IX that the manuscript was written on the back of.) Grothendieck is identifying a group-valued functor Ω on rings k with an explicit affine group scheme over Z.

1. Rings involved.
- Ŝ_k = k{{T}} is the completed divided-power series ring in one variable T over k.
- Ŝ_k{{X_0}} is the completed divided-power series ring in a further variable X_0 over Ŝ_k.

2. Description of Ω(k). An element of Ω(k) is a system (A, (B_i)_{i≥1}) where
- A = Σ_{j≥1} a_j X_0^{[j]}, a PD series with no constant term, i.e. a candidate image of the generator X_0 under a continuous PD-endomorphism;
- B_i = Σ_{j≥0} b_{ij} X_0^{[j]}, with b_{ij} in Ŝ_k.
The conditions are:
- (a) the augmentation ε(a_1) of the linear coefficient is a unit of k. This is the usual invertibility criterion for a substitution X_0 ↦ A(X_0) to be an automorphism; Grothendieck writes it as Δ(φ_{·1}), a Jacobian/derivative.
- (b) 2B_i = 0. Such 2-torsion typically comes from components acting on odd-degree generators in a strictly graded-commutative PD algebra over Z.

3. Expansion in coordinates. Expanding a_j = Σ_h a_{jh} T^{[h]} and b_{ij} = Σ_h b_{ijh} T^{[h]} gives arbitrary families with a_{10} ∈ k^× and 2b_{ijh} = 0. Hence Ω is representable by the affine Z-scheme
Spec( Z[(A_{jh}), (B_{ijh})] / (2B_{ijh}) )[A_{10}^{-1}].
As a scheme this is G_m × G_a^{(N*×N)∖{(1,0)}} × (₂G_a)^{N*×N×N}, where ₂G_a = Spec Z[x]/(2x) is the 2-torsion of G_a.

4. Group structure and interpretation. The group law (composition of substitutions) is not the product law of these factors. Ω is a non-flat affine group scheme over Z, and Grothendieck interprets it as the automorphism group scheme of a functor: roughly, from Z-algebras to (simplicial) PD differential k-algebras homotopic to Â. The final lines are hard to read.

The purpose is apparently to compute the 'symmetry group' of the PD de Rham model (a universal PD dga over Z). The T-variable seems to account for homotopies or the simplicial direction. This links to his idea that PD de Rham complexes over Z model homotopy types, which reappears later as 'schematization' in Pursuing Stacks.
errors: As transcribed, the product decomposition puts a 2-torsion factor ₂G_a^{N*×N} on the A-coefficients. The stated conditions impose 2-torsion only on the b_{ijh}. The a_{jh} for (j,h) ≠ (1,0) are free, so that factor should be G_a^{(N*×N)∖{(1,0)}}, with a_{10} supplying the G_m factor. Either a slip of the pen or a misreading of the handwriting.

The scheme isomorphism Ω ≅ G_m × G_a^... × ₂G_a^... holds only as schemes. The group law is substitution/composition, which the notes do not spell out; calling Ω a group scheme rests on this unwritten composition law.
The defining functor in the last lines ('automorphismes du foncteur ... simpliciales homotopes à Â') is only partially legible and not made precise.

ideas.what: Describing automorphisms of a completed PD power-series algebra by substitution series X_0 ↦ Σ a_j X_0^{[j]} with invertible linear term, and representing the resulting group functor by an explicit affine group scheme over Z
ideas.modern_name: Group scheme of coordinate changes of the formal PD line (Aut of Ĝ_a^♯-type objects); analogue of the group of formal coordinate changes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Coordinate-change group schemes: Lazard/Quillen/Landweber–Novikov tradition (1950s–70s). Automorphisms of G_a^♯: Drinfeld, Bhatt–Lurie (2020s)
ideas.where_published: PD de Rham theory was publicly discussed only via Berthelot/Illusie; no published version of this talk is known to me

ideas.what: Appearance of 2-torsion (non-flat) factors ₂G_a in the automorphism group of a PD differential graded algebra over Z, from components acting on odd-degree generators
ideas.modern_name: Non-flatness of automorphism group schemes of strictly graded-commutative PD dgas over Z; prime-2 phenomena in cochain models
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; related phenomena appear in work on integral/p-adic cochain models (Mandell, Toën's affine stacks)

ideas.what: Interpreting Ω as the automorphism group of a functor towards simplicial PD differential algebras up to homotopy, i.e. symmetries of a PD de Rham model of homotopy types over Z
ideas.modern_name: Automorphisms of the (PD) de Rham / cochain functor; schematization of homotopy types, affine stacks
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses schematization but not, to my knowledge, this explicit group

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly computes the automorphism group scheme Ω over Z of a PD de Rham-type structure. It is a non-flat affine group scheme with a G_m × G_a^∞ part and 2-torsion ₂G_a^∞ factors, and he proposes it as the automorphism group of a functor to simplicial PD differential algebras up to homotopy. The intended application, presumably the action of these symmetries on PD de Rham models of homotopy types over Z, is not completed here.
missed.quote: Ainsi Ω peut être considéré comme un schéma en groupes sur Z, qui est le schéma des automorphismes du foncteur ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Current work on integral models of homotopy types touches the same 'symmetries of the de Rham functor' question: affine stacks, filtered circles, G_a^♯ and its automorphisms in prismatization. An explicit 1976 computation of such a group, with its prime-2 torsion, would be of historical interest and possibly a useful test case.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation itself is routine (coordinate-change group of a PD power-series algebra). What is notable is the 1976 framing as the automorphism group scheme over Z of a PD de Rham / simplicial-homotopy functor, with explicit 2-torsion, which anticipates later schematization and G_a^♯ themes. It is fragmentary and partly illegible, though.
transcription_corrections: 'Z[F(A_{jh})...]': the 'F' looks like a stray or struck mark; read Z[(A_{jh})_{j≥1,h≥0}, (B_{ijh})_{i≥1,j≥0,h≥0}].
'localisé du plus p.d. à A_{1,0}' should probably read 'localisé par rapport à A_{1,0}' (i.e. A_{10} inverted).
The first power factor should likely read G_a^{N*×N} (not ₂G_a), matching the stated conditions.
'ε(a_1) (= Δ(φ_{·1}))': Δ is possibly a determinant/Jacobian symbol; reading uncertain.
Final lines are mostly illegible; 'homotopes à Â' is conjectural.
